background.description: What the learner has previously encountered, per domain. Ask WHAT they have studied, never HOW WELL: self-rated knowledge gain correlates about zero with measured gain and self-reported level runs consistently high, while learners do reliably remember which courses, books and projects they went through. So level here is a hypothesis to be probed, never a reason to skip probing.

registers.description: Language register PER DOMAIN. The same learner is terse-technical in one field and analogy-first in another; one global setting is the root cause of explanations that are either over-simplified or over-hard.

domain.description: Use an asterisk as the domain name for the fallback register.

basis.description: Why this domain needs this register, preferably the learner's own words.

source_languages.description: Languages the learner can read source material in. Distinct from teaching_language in config.

constraints.description: Standing learner constraints, for example no video material, or formulas must be LaTeX.

purpose.description: Why this person is learning. Asked at first setup because it is the one thing that cannot be measured later, and it sets how deep is deep enough.

depth_expectation.description: Default depth target for new courses: 1 can-use, 2 can-compute, 3 can-derive, 4 can-critique, 5 can-create. A standing answer to how far to push, so it is not renegotiated every lesson.

notation_input.description: How this learner can supply notation, asked once and then honoured. It sits here rather than in the free-text constraints list because a constraint written as prose cannot be checked against an item: `formulas must be LaTeX` reads clearly and gates nothing.
